intro: You've searched for the best EIS help near you — probably because you're raising money under the Enterprise Investment Scheme, or thinking about investing through it, and you want expert guidance to get the reliefs right. Getting EIS wrong can be costly, so finding a tax adviser who truly understands the scheme is a sensible step.
need_heading: What people searching for EIS help usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for EIS help are either company founders raising funds or investors wanting to use the reliefs — and both need accurate, specialist advice.
needs: You're a founder planning to raise money under EIS and need to ensure your company qualifies and that investors can claim relief.
You're an investor considering an EIS investment and want to understand how the reliefs work and what records you'll need to keep.
You've already issued EIS shares and need help completing the compliance paperwork correctly so investors don't lose their relief.
You're unsure whether your company should use EIS or SEIS, and you want advice on which scheme fits your circumstances.
You've had a query from HMRC about an EIS investment and need a tax adviser to help you respond.
context_heading: Understanding EIS and finding the right help
context: The Enterprise Investment Scheme offers tax reliefs to investors who buy shares in qualifying companies, but the rules are detailed and mistakes can cost investors their relief. A tax adviser who works with EIS regularly can help you navigate the conditions and paperwork.

When searching for the best help near you, it's worth checking a professional's qualifications and experience. 'Tax adviser' isn't a protected title, so look for membership of bodies like the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians, and ask about their approach to EIS.

Your location and whether you'd prefer to meet in person or work remotely, to help us find someone near you.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the tax adviser
questions: What experience do you have with the Enterprise Investment Scheme?
Are you a member of the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians?
How do you keep up to date with changes to EIS rules?
What records should I keep for EIS purposes, and for how long?
Can you help with both EIS and SEIS if needed?
What are your fees, and how will you keep me informed throughout the process?

faqs.q: What is the Enterprise Investment Scheme?
faqs.a: The Enterprise Investment Scheme is a UK government scheme that offers tax reliefs to investors who buy shares in qualifying companies. It's designed to help smaller companies raise finance.

faqs.q: Do I need a tax adviser for EIS?
faqs.a: While not compulsory, a tax adviser can help ensure you meet the conditions and claim reliefs correctly. Mistakes can be costly, so professional guidance is often wise.

faqs.q: How can I check a tax adviser's credentials?
faqs.a: Look for membership of professional bodies such as the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians. You can also ask about their experience and qualifications directly.

faqs.q: Can iComply recommend a specific tax adviser?
faqs.a: iComply introduces you to a suitable UK professional based on your needs, but we don't recommend or endorse any particular adviser. You should satisfy yourself that they are right for you.

extra_heading: Weighing up EIS help when "best" means something personal
extra: Searching for the "best EIS help near me" tells us less about rankings and more about fit: you want someone close enough to talk things through easily, who deals with the Enterprise Investment Scheme often enough to spot the details that matter. There is no official league table of EIS advisers, so "best" really comes down to what you check for yourself. A nearby adviser you can actually reach is worth more than a distant name that sounds impressive.

When you compare options, ask each one to walk you through a scenario close to yours — a founder checking whether the company's trade qualifies, or an investor working out what records to keep after shares are issued. Listen for specific answers about EIS conditions and the SEIS alternative, and notice whether they ask you questions about your circumstances before offering a view. Ask too about their qualifications, their anti-money-laundering supervision and their professional indemnity insurance, since paid tax advisers must be supervised and it is reasonable to check before you go ahead.

At a first appointment, expect to explain whether you are raising money or investing, what the company does, and the stage you have reached, such as whether shares have already been issued. A good adviser will set out what they need from you, how they will keep you informed and how their fees work, with quotes given on application rather than fixed in advance. If something in their answers feels vague, that is worth noting — mistakes in EIS paperwork can cost investors their relief, so clarity early on matters.

extra_faqs.q: Does "near me" mean I need to meet an EIS adviser face to face?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Many people work with a tax adviser by phone, email or video, and proximity can simply mean someone in your area who is easy to reach. When you tell iComply your location and how you would prefer to work, we can introduce you to a suitable UK professional on that basis.

extra_faqs.q: How can I tell whether an EIS adviser is really experienced with the scheme?
extra_faqs.a: Ask them to describe how they handle the qualifying conditions, the paperwork when shares are issued and the choice between EIS and SEIS, and see whether their answers are concrete. Checking membership of the Chartered Institute of Taxation or the Association of Taxation Technicians, along with their supervision and insurance, gives you a clearer picture than any claim to be the best.
